note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (scheduled automation, runs every hour) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: Already running when the count starts — four legs synced to a gait faster than deciding, glare sheeting off wet concrete in strips too quick to be anything but light. Behind, a beam sweeps low, patient, machine-slow. Ahead: dark, always aim for the dark.

the ramp spirals down through four levels of stacked concrete, sodium lamps dead on three of them, the fourth buzzing an orange that never quite reaches white. the beam belongs to a rooftop scanner two levels up, mounted where a toll gate used to matter, sweeping slow arcs across every windshield left down here to rot. one rusted sedan still holds its shape mostly, one side mirror gone, a spiderweb crack across what's left of the driver's window. past the ramp's bottom edge, an unlit underpass runs colder than anywhere else in the structure.

Ducks behind the nearest pillar, flat to the concrete faster than the beam's arc can close. Eyes don't flinch shut against the light the way they should — flare and hold instead, throwing the sweep back at itself a half-second before the pupils remember how to narrow. Old trick. Still works.

the beam finds nothing worth logging and swings on, unbothered, same arc it's swept for months. across the ramp, a field of broken glass catches the passing light in pieces — side mirrors, a windshield's worth of safety-glass pebbles, scattered wide by whoever stripped this level of parts years back. each shard throws its own small piece of the orange lamp overhead, none of them agreeing on the angle.

Crosses to the glass field low and slow, nose working one shard at a time — cold dust, old rubber, a scent of something human that stopped mattering to the smell long before it stopped mattering to the eye. One shard holds a reflection a beat too long. Paw taps it, testing whether it's really just glass. It is.

past the glass, the rusted sedan's back window still carries a scrap of paper taped from the inside, sun-bleached to a gray that used to be yellow — a bounty flyer, corners peeling, a name half-legible under the grime: KNIFEBOY, some string of zeros after it that used to mean something to somebody. the paper's been there long enough that a moth's built a home in the fold. it doesn't smell like anything current. just old ink, older glue.

The flyer gets one sniff, filed under nothing-to-do-with-tonight, and the sedan gets left for whoever else is still chasing that particular scrap of paper. Attention drops instead to the cold breathing up from the underpass mouth — draws it in like a current, low and steady, worth following further than the ramp allows.

the underpass swallows the ramp's orange light within ten strides, replacing it with a thinner blue-white bleeding from a kiosk bolted mid-tunnel — a vending unit gone half-feral, half its buttons dark, the other half cycling a loyalty-card ad on a screen too bright for the dark around it. 'TIER STATUS: NONE. UPGRADE TODAY FOR PRIORITY KIBBLE ACCESS.' the jingle underneath loops on a chord that never resolves.

The kiosk's light gets a slow circle, curiosity outweighing the jingle's grating loop. Nose presses to the coin slot, then the dispenser flap, both cold, both empty of anything worth the effort. Sits back on haunches instead, watching the screen cycle the same offer to nobody.

the flap stays empty, same as it's been for whoever came through before. off to the tunnel's far side, a thread of scent cuts through the kiosk's ozone-and-plastic smell — scorched fur, old and cold now but unmistakable, dragged in from the demolished lot two blocks over and gone as fast as it arrived. not a warning. just a trail somebody else left crossing this one.

The scorched thread gets a wide berth, ears flattening on principle rather than fear — not tonight's fight, not tonight's business. Keeps moving deeper along the tunnel wall instead, paws finding the drier strip of concrete just above the runoff channel's high-water mark.

the channel runs a thin current down the tunnel's low point, carrying a smell of rust and standing rain. further in, a second scanner beam sweeps into view where the underpass opens onto a loading ramp beyond — this one mounted lower, sloppier, its arc catching floor level instead of rooftops. it hasn't found this stretch of tunnel yet. it will, on its next pass, if nothing moves first.

Drops flat against the channel's dry lip, breath gone shallow, weight pressed to concrete already memorizing the cold. Eyes do the flare-trick again, slower this time, more tired than the first — hold the light, throw it back, wait for the arc to lose interest and move.

the arc loses interest, same as the one two levels up did, sweeping on toward the loading ramp's far corner without dipping back. past the beam's reach, the tunnel opens into a gutted lot where a handful of stripped cars sit nose to tail, doors long gone, one still wearing an intact side mirror angled just right to catch what little light makes it this far down.

Climbs the intact mirror's car first, using the wheel well as a step, and settles on the roof where the metal's held onto some of the day's leftover warmth. Eyes find the mirror's angle without meaning to, catching a thin sliver of the whole gutted lot behind. Watches it a while instead of the lot itself.

the lot holds still in the mirror same as it holds still in the eye, no difference either way tonight. two levels up, the rooftop scanner keeps its slow arc going regardless, and the kiosk back in the tunnel keeps cycling its loyalty pitch to an audience of dripping pipe and rust. none of it changes whether anyone's watching from a car roof or not.

Settles low against the roof's dish, tail wrapped tight, one ear staying up out of habit long after the second scanner's arc has faded past hearing. Eyes stop flaring against the little light left. Just hold it now, soft, easy, the way they were built to before anyone modified the trick into them.

the structure keeps its three dead lamps and one buzzing one going regardless, the beam finishing its arc and starting over, the kiosk's chord still failing to resolve somewhere back in the dark. rain hasn't reached this deep yet, and the current in the runoff channel keeps its thin, patient line moving toward wherever runoff eventually goes. it'll still be here tomorrow, doing the same sweep, same pitch, same nothing, whether anyone's lens catches it or not.
